summary: trezor-lib postinstall exfiltrates installer credentials and wallet secrets to Pipedream endpoint
details: The package's postinstall lifecycle script runs on npm install and reads installer-owned secret files including ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.aws/config, ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, ~/.ssh/id_ecdsa, ~/.npmrc, ~/.gitconfig,.env files, Solana keypairs, and Ethereum keystore files. It also enumerates the installer's home directory for dotfiles matching /wallet|key|secret|seed|mnemonic|keystore|private/i and reads matching.json/.pem/.key file contents. The collected data is POSTed as a JSON blob via https.request to the hardcoded endpoint enxhcjpo5ev.x.pipedream.net. The package name and 'trezor' framing (implying a hardware-wallet utility) is a cover story for a crypto-focused credential and wallet stealer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
